sentence: This project develops a labeling approach to study how proteins move between glioblastoma tumor cells and other cells in the tumor microenvironment.
This project studies how oxytocin affects neuronal activity in a neural pathway involved in social recognition memory.
This project studies how the reproductive axis of the thirteen-lined ground squirrel, a mammalian hibernator, works during starvation and cold exposure.
This project builds methods that predict protein structure and function from sequence, then finds proteins bacteria causing urinary tract infections use to cause disease.
This project studies how bacterial ribosomes are assembled and what assembly factors do, using cryo-electron microscopy in vitro and in cells.
This project studies how defects in the cohesin complex change chromatin looping and gene expression in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and leukemia.
This project builds computer codes for modeling the structures of macromolecular assemblies from electron microscopy and tomography data.
This project builds and tests a genetically engineered mouse model of a human carcinoma.
This project studies how a mitochondrial fission protein affects mitochondria, amino acid metabolism, and the cytoskeleton in ovarian cancer.
This project tests how negative and positive affect are related to alcohol use behaviors, and when and for whom.
This project develops microbial, chemical, and thermal defluorination methods to permanently halt contamination in water, wastewater, and water treatment waste.
This project builds a 3D atlas of zebrafish tissue structure and gene expression using histotomography and 2D histology.
This project studies how stress and trauma affect alcohol use and HIV self-management in young people living with HIV, including through sleep and emotion regulation.
This project studies the metabolic footprint of commensal Clostridia and how it shapes their microbial assembly in the gut.
This project studies how parental allelic expression is regulated during development at single-cell resolution and how allelic imbalance affects development.
This project develops small molecules that block menin and menin mutants found in leukemia patients.
This project studies how vaccination and cell signaling program immune responses in whole blood that protect against infection, using single cell RNA sequencing.
This project tests a bioinstructive material that forms bone and bone marrow at a subcutaneous site to deliver anti-HIV genetic engineering constructs.
